clue.text: Actress Joan needs resolve, getting the bird

parts.note: Joan Greenwood was a British film actress of the 1940s and 50s
pecker is old British slang for courage or resolve, as in 'keep your pecker up'

explanation.surface: A film star called Joan is told to toughen up and is given the bird by her audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' suggests being booed, but 'the bird' is the definition. 'Keep your pecker up' is a British idiom meaning stay resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodpecker is a common European species, so the phrase names a particular bird.

clue.text: Went through water to jetty, getting more sodden

parts.note: swam is the past tense of swim, moving through water
a pier is a jetty projecting into the sea

explanation.surface: A swimmer heads for the jetty and gets wetter and wetter.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of swampy: boggier, wetter, so more sodden fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Material is black when consumed by flames

indicators.note: being consumed by means being swallowed inside, so the black letter goes within the flames word

parts.note: flames make a fire
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Some fabric turns black when it catches fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibre can mean a textile or material made of threads, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Trainee medics in theatre performances, we hear?

indicators.note: a signal that the words are to be judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act in variety theatre, so 'in turns' is in theatre performances

explanation.surface: Junior hospital doctors are rumoured to be appearing on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turns' and the answer are pronounced alike; a 'turn' is a music-hall act.
explanation.definitionFit: Internes is an older or American spelling for junior hospital doctors still in training.

clue.text: Nymph to finish up hugging Herbert

indicators.note: hugging means holding something within, so the writer's initials sit inside
in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: finish means end
A. P. Herbert, the English humorist and MP, was widely known by his initials APH

explanation.surface: A request to wrap things up while giving someone called Herbert a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Herbert look like a man being hugged, but the humorist A. P. Herbert signed himself by his initials; 'up' reverses because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is the nymph of Greek myth who was turned into a laurel tree to escape Apollo.

clue.text: River's rising around derelict fort in theatrical place

indicators.note: around signals one piece placed about another, the river's letters going round the ruined fort
in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, here with the possessive S

indicators.note: derelict means ruined and broken down, so the letters of fort are disordered

explanation.surface: A river climbs around a ruined fort in a town famous for its theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a Devon river; 'rising' reads it upwards in this down clue, and 'derelict' scrambles fort before 'around' wraps the river's letters round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratford-upon-Avon is Shakespeare's birthplace and home of the Royal Shakespeare Company, a theatrical town.

clue.text: Expecting a hack to provide gen on almost everything

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another means it sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A journalist is expected to supply information on nearly every subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist, but it is a horse for riding, so 'expecting a hack' is a pregnant mare's state. 'Gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare carrying an unborn horse is said to be in foal, so expecting a young horse.

clue.text: Expertise is disguised with prim aloofness

indicators.note: disguised means made to look different, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Competence can be hidden behind a prim and aloof manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' shuffles IS plus PRIM ALOOFNESS; 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionalism is the skill and competence expected of a trained practitioner, which is expertise.

clue.text: Natural earth woman is fighting back

indicators.note: back means the whole run of woman, is and fighting is read in reverse

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A woman takes up arms to defend the natural world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole sentence 'Anne is war' around, not just one word; 'Natural earth' is a pigment, not soil.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a brownish-yellow pigment made from natural clay, an earth colour used by painters.

clue.text: Outside front of radio this could be something rotating

definitions.text: Outside front of radio this could be something rotating

indicators.note: read as out-side, putting a letter outside the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a turner is a thing that turns or rotates

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A knob on the outside of a radio set that you twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' is read as 'put out', removing R ('front of radio') from TURNER. The whole clue also describes a radio's rotating knob.
explanation.definitionFit: On a radio the tuning control is often a dial that rotates, so a radio part.

clue.text: Film studio — male not special, is wooden

indicators.note: male not special means the male letter stands where the special letter was

parts.note: Elstree, north of London, is home to famous British film studios

explanation.surface: A film studio's leading man is not special and acts woodenly.
explanation.walkthrough: ELSTREE is a British film studio; swapping S for M gives the answer. The surface suggests a stiff actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose definition: this tree is made of wood, so it may be described as wooden.

clue.text: What the Queen of Hearts wanted to avoid

definitions.text: What the Queen of Hearts wanted
definitions.meaning: in Alice in Wonderland the Queen of Hearts keeps shouting 'Off with her head!'
to stop something happening by acting first, intercept

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to block or forestall, and literally describes a beheading the Queen demanded.

clue.text: Effect when horse gets in gorse

indicators.note: horse gets in means the horse letter enters the other word

parts.note: to effect a result is to bring it about, to win it
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A horse wanders into some gorse with consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect' is a verb here (to bring about, win), and 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Whin is a dialect name for gorse, the spiny yellow-flowered shrub.

clue.text: Perhaps the devil is cast out somewhere in Venezuela

definitions.text: Perhaps the devil is cast out
definitions.meaning: the devil was once an angel thrown out of heaven, so a heavenly being tumbles
the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall is in Venezuela

explanation.definitionFit: The highest waterfall in the world is in Venezuela, and the phrase also describes Lucifer's fall from heaven.

clue.text: Wild green site

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of green site are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An untamed stretch of grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges GREEN SITE, and the whole clue describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tanzanian national park is a vast grassland wilderness, a wild green site.

clue.text: Loses out crossing a river without rower?

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so one piece is placed within the other
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of loses are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loses out while trying to cross a river with no one rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LOSES as OLESS, and 'crossing' sets A and R inside after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Without oars at all is the literal meaning; the question mark flags the playful link to having no rower.

clue.text: String player not good person — or inspired musician

indicators.note: inspired literally means breathed in, so the word or is taken inside
not means without, so the good person's letters are dropped

parts.note: a cellist plays a stringed instrument
ST, for saint, stands for a good person

explanation.surface: A violinist is no saint, or else an inspired musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the saint from the player; 'inspired' means breathed in, so the word or is taken inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque composer and violinist, so a musician.

clue.text: Mathematical function — feel comfortable with the jargon?

parts.note: to cose is an old verb meaning to make oneself cosy
cant is the special jargon of a group

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are at ease with mathematical terminology.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosecant is the trigonometric function, reciprocal of the sine.

clue.text: Herefordshire town somehow set out to bring in old stars

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so the old letter is placed within
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of set may be taken in any order
out means removed, so the letters of set leave the town's name

parts.note: Leominster is a market town in Herefordshire, in the west of England
the letters of set, in the order they stand in the town name

explanation.surface: A Herefordshire town sets out to take in ancient stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' lets the letters of set leave the town's name in any order, 'out' removes them, and 'to bring in' adds the old letter near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Minor, the Little Lion, is a small constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Petrol cap's possibly something that comes with the van

definitions.text: something that comes with the van

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may form something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: here the 's gives a letter, cap plus S

explanation.surface: A petrol cap might arrive with a van delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PETROL CAPS. The parcel service is delivered by van.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcels sent by post arrive on a delivery van, so this is something that comes with the van.

clue.text: I help with gigs — I adore travelling

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of I adore are shifted

explanation.surface: A music fan who loves going on tour helps out at concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges I ADORE, and a roadie travels with the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie sets up equipment for bands on tour, helping with gigs.

clue.text: Ceremonial procession gets soldier half dead

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: half picks the first two of the four letters of dead

explanation.surface: A soldier at a ceremonial march is half dead with exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a formal march past or procession, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Nothing for fellow to eat? There's beef

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so the nothing letter goes inside

parts.note: man means fellow
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A man with nothing to eat complains about having no beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like food, but it is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a complaint or grumble, a synonym in its informal sense.

clue.text: What Esau took from Jacob without hesitation?

definitions.text: What Esau took from Jacob without hesitation?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation letters are removed

parts.note: Jacob was Esau's twin brother in Genesis
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Esau, famished, seized his brother's stew in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for a dish of pottage, a stew; BROTHER without ER gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical pottage Esau accepted was a thick stew or soup, a broth.

clue.text: Slip caught Aussie opener

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Justin Langer was an Australian Test cricket opening batsman

explanation.surface: An Australian opening batsman is caught in the slips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like the cricket fielding position, but it is the definition: a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is British slang for an embarrassing mistake, a slip.

clue.text: Friendly face met with expression of surprise

indicators.note: met with joins the face word to the exclamation, which stands in front of it

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
dial is slang for a face

explanation.surface: A friendly face is greeted with a gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation; 'dial' is slang for face.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly in manner, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Be established as keeper for team?

indicators.note: a keeper holds something, so the established letters hold the team inside

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Someone is confirmed as the team's goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeper' suggests a goalkeeper, but here the established letters keep the team inside them; XI for eleven players is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to exist, both meaning to have being.

clue.text: Races after party to get presents

indicators.note: after places the races word behind the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
nations are races or peoples

explanation.surface: After a party, various peoples receive gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Donations are gifts given, so presents in the noun sense.
